topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its key learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the principles, applications, systemic toxicities, and resistance mechanisms of standard non-targeted cancer modalities, including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Targeting cancer-specific cellular vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore strategies to selectively target cancer cells by exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities such as hormone dependency, checkpoint deficiencies, oncolytic viral sensitivity, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Oncogene-targeted therapies and kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale behind targeting oncogenic driver mutations, the development of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and the emergence of drug resistance and addiction mechanisms.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the use of engineered monoclonal antibodies to block tumor surface receptors, recruit immune effector mechanisms, and deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular immune modulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biological basis of tumor immunosurveillance and evaluate therapeutic methods to activate antitumor T cell responses, including checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesise the ongoing challenges of tumor heterogeneity and resistance, historical treatment successes, and future paradigms in oncology.
